single.prompt: Revenue trend for the FinBridge board. Monthly card spend processed (£m): Jan 18, Feb 19, Mar 22, Apr 21, May 26, Jun 31, Jul 30, Aug 36. Need to explain the June jump (Xero integration launch) and the July dip (seasonality).
Show how our churn cohort curves differ: the 2024 cohorts retain much better after month 3, and I want to call out why (onboarding redesign, shift to annual plans).
UK grocery market share 2019-2025, discounters vs the big four. Point out the year they cross over and the two drivers behind it.

Unit economics of our three plans side by side (price / gross margin / CAC / payback months): Starter £0 / 42% / £180 / 14; Growth £49 / 61% / £420 / 9; Scale £199 / 68% / £1,900 / 11. Point out Growth is the sweet spot and Scale payback is inflated by enterprise sales cost.
FinBridge vs Pleo, Soldo and Spendesk on FX fee, monthly fee per user and credit line. Then what it means for our positioning.
Store P&L for the four pilot stores: sales, labour %, shrink %. I need to explain why Leeds underperforms despite the best top line.
Slide arguing that UK SMEs lose real money to manual expense reconciliation. Our survey says the average SME spends £11,400 a year in finance staff time on it.
I need to convince the board the addressable market is big enough: UK SMEs with 10-249 employees put £84bn a year through business cards. That's the point of the slide.
Churn slide for the SaaS review. The story: 62% of churned accounts never activated an integration. NPS is 41 and support tickets are up 12%, but the activation stat is the story.
Walk through the 18-month ERP rollout plan: design, build, pilot, rollout, hypercare.
How a FinBridge expense flows from tap to ledger: card tap, receipt capture, auto-categorisation, approval, sync to Xero.
The client's M&A history: bought Northway in 2016, Cardell in 2019, merged with Vesta in 2022, carved out the services arm in 2025.
Three strategic options for the board: build organically, acquire a payroll player, or partner with a bank. One line on each.
The four pillars of our people strategy: attract, develop, reward, retain.
Headline results from the pilot: 23% fewer stockouts, £1.4m working capital released, 4.2pts margin uplift. Three wins, all of them matter.
MRR chart: Jan 42k, Feb 48k, Mar 55k, Apr 71k, May 78k, Jun 96k. The April jump is our Xero app launch and June is our first enterprise logo; investors will ask.
Weekly active clinics since launch. There are three spikes I need to explain: the NHS framework win, our webinar with the RCGP, and the BMJ feature.
CAC by channel over the last 4 quarters: paid social 40, 55, 72, 95; referral 20, 21, 19, 20; SEO 35, 28, 22, 18. Investors need to see why we're moving budget and what's behind each line.
Unit economics, SMB vs mid-market: ACV £6k vs £28k, gross margin 78% vs 81%, CAC £4.5k vs £14k, payback 11 vs 7 months. Investors need to see why we're doubling down on mid-market.
Use of funds for the £4m raise: engineering £1.8m, sales £1.2m, marketing £0.6m, G&A £0.4m, with the hires and milestone each unlocks. Add a line on why engineering is the biggest bucket.
Competition slide: us vs Pleo, Soldo, Spendesk and Amex on credit line, automatic receipts, Xero sync and price per user.
Problem slide: UK SMEs waste 9 hours a month chasing receipts. That's the whole point.
Market slide: £84bn of SME card spend in the UK. Investors should get it in one glance.
Traction: we hit £1.2m ARR, up from £300k a year ago. We also have 140 customers and 3 sales reps, but ARR is what matters.
Roadmap: Q1 expense cards, Q2 bill pay, Q3 credit line, Q4 EU expansion.
How it works: sign up in 5 minutes, issue cards, snap receipts, books close themselves.
Our story so far: founded 2023 in Leeds, first pilot hospital 2024, NHS framework 2025, Series A 2026.
Traction slide: £2.4m ARR, 310 customers, 128% NRR, zero churned logos this year.
Three products, one platform: cards, bill pay, credit.
Before vs after FinBridge: 3 days to close the month, now 3 hours.

consulting.prompt: A&E performance across our 12 trusts, % seen within 4 hours. I want to flag the three outliers and what they have in common.
How gross margin went from 38% to 31%: interchange cut -3pts, fraud losses -2, FX mix -1.5, pricing +0.5, other -1. Explain each of the big drivers briefly.
Client emissions by scope, 2020-2025. The board must see scope 3 is 80% and growing, and that scope 1-2 progress comes mostly from grid decarbonisation, not their own action.
Freight cost per pallet by lane over the last 8 quarters. The Midlands lanes diverged after the Coventry depot closure; annotate that quarter.
Attrition by tenure band: <1y 34%, 1-2y 22%, 2-5y 14%, 5y+ 7%. Want to call out that first-year attrition is concentrated in two regions and exit surveys blame onboarding.
Marketplace GMV vs take rate, 2021-2026. Take rate fell from 14% to 11% while GMV tripled; explain that this was a deliberate trade-off and what it bought us.
SME card adoption by company size: adoption jumps at 20+ employees, and I want to note that the under-10 segment still uses personal cards.
Results of the pricing test, conversion by tier: £29 7.1%, £39 6.8%, £49 4.2%, £59 3.9%. Highlight the cliff between 39 and 49 and what it means for how we package plans.
Show UK SME card spend: 2019 £61bn, 2020 £55bn, 2021 £66bn, 2022 £72bn, 2023 £78bn, 2024 £84bn. The message is it recovered and has grown ~8% a year since 2021.
Slide with the NHS elective waiting list since 2015. It's the obvious hockey stick, no commentary needed.

pitch.prompt: Revenue slide: 2022 £0.2m, 2023 £0.9m, 2024 £2.6m, 2025 £6.1m. Just show it going up.
Retention curves for marketplace buyers by cohort. Cohorts after we launched same-day delivery retain 2x better; that's our best argument.
Show GMV compounding since launch, 15% month on month for 14 months.
Us vs competitors on FX fees: us 0%, Amex 2.99%, high-street banks 2.75%, Pleo 1.5%. Make it obvious we're cheapest.
10-year cumulative cost: our solar-as-a-service vs buying panels outright vs doing nothing. Point is we're cheaper from year 2.
Slide showing our burn multiple improving every quarter this year: 3.1, 2.4, 1.8, 1.2.
UK home-care market 2020 to 2030 forecast. Big and growing, that's all.
Pricing: Starter free, Team £8/user, Business £15/user, Enterprise custom, with seats, integrations and support level for each.
Cap table summary for the data room: founders, ESOP, angels, seed fund, with shares held, % pre-money and % post-money.
